style: prop (Trillium), discretionary intraday, capitulation/reversal and breakout specialist
edge_principles: Broken slot machine: each day only ~5-10 names in the whole market offer real edge; trade those rather than a fixed favourite niche, and pick the most extreme instance of a theme (biggest dislocation vs its driver/the index).
Require alignment across timeframes (intraday and daily both a buy) before taking a trade; skip when the move is already too extended for the with-trend side.
Judge moves by price over time (speed/size of the move) plus volume capitulation, not by price level alone.
Grade setups A/B/C and pre-set risk per grade on a card; stop trading C setups entirely and scale risk exponentially (not linearly) on A/A+ setups.
Default stop is the prior bar low (long) / prior bar high (short) on the short intraday chart.
The same price has different expected value at different moments: a breakout or news reaction bought late after it has come back is a worse trade than the first print.
Do not exit at the first higher-low pullback after a confirmed breakout; give the trade to the real low (channel fundamentals).
Process: one-goal daily report card, detailed write-ups and screen recordings of only the biggest plays, mentor feedback; lockouts after ~3 losing trades to avoid tilt.
notes: Part 3 interview recorded June 2022: broken slot machine stock selection, right side of the V capitulation entries, channel fundamentals and exponential bet sizing. Mentions an index stat: ~30 historical cases of a 10% Nasdaq drop in 3 days showed a positive bounce edge.

style: journalist/author (biography of bond fund manager Bill Gross, PIMCO)
edge_principles: Structural alpha: small, repeatable basis-point edges from contract details (e.g. investing idle cash collateral behind futures in short floating notes) compound over years.
Read new contracts carefully: newly launched products can carry embedded options that nobody has priced for an untested regime.
Risk down early into a perceived bubble and accept underperformance; the payoff is having dry powder to buy forced sellers' assets at a discount.
Size and new-issue allocation can be an edge in bond markets, unlike in nimble equity trading.
notes: Author interview about PIMCO and Bill Gross history (GNMA futures trade, 2008 GSE bet, 2014 departure). No intraday setups.

guest: Public Service Announcement (Aaron Fifield, Tessa Dao)
edge_principles: New co-host attributes her turnaround to reviewing her own trades, managing risk better, simplifying and trading less, and not relying solely on trading income (reduces pressure).
notes: Host transition announcement; co-host briefly mentions neutral multi-leg options trades around earnings. No concrete setups.

style: retail, discretionary intraday large-cap equities (formerly options scalper)
edge_principles: Keep a position-size table next to the screen: account value x risk% / stop distance gives shares instantly; size grows organically with the account.
Default risk 0.5% per trade, 1% only on the best setups; cutting risk in half from 1% fixed his inability to hold trades.
Top-down prep: indexes (SPX, QQQ, IWM, Dow) then sector ETFs (XLE, XLK) to find who leads/lags, then names with catalysts.
Tighten stops in equities to keep reward:risk >= 3-4:1 on realistic intraday ranges.
In choppy bear tape avoid both chasing breakouts and pressing shorts after big declines; fade strength into levels instead.
Most P&L comes from the first couple of hours after the open.
notes: First-year full-time retail trader; ~50% win rate with ~30% scratches. Mostly round-number and post-run fades in large caps.

style: retail/educator (Simpler Trading), discretionary options swing and day trader
edge_principles: Only trade a stock if it is outperforming the index; otherwise just trade the index. On down days scan for stocks that are up and vice versa.

Know when big 'focus trades' are available (strong index + strong stocks, as in 2020-21) and do not force them in choppy regimes; switch to day trading / small weekly goals when swing trades stop working.
'True/false statement': stay in a losing-but-valid setup as long as the original reasons remain true and risk is within plan; exit when a reason becomes false.
Traders tend to make money in the morning and give it back in the afternoon (impatience, decision fatigue); step away from screens.
Never hold directional trades through earnings; momentum often runs into earnings, not through them.
Scale into high-conviction trades (start ~5%, build toward 25-30% of account) using defined-risk spreads so the position can survive sideways chop.
A paper loss equals a real loss; cut non-working trades rather than waiting to get back to even.
Skim profits into illiquid tangible assets so a drawdown cannot give back everything.
notes: Follow-up interview on his 2020-21 big options trades (Tesla, Google). Core setup: relative strength vs weak index + daily squeeze, target 3 ATR Keltner.

style: former CME eurodollar options / NYMEX nat gas floor trader; now discretionary VIX term-structure vs ES trader
markets: rates options, natural gas, VIX futures, ES futures
edge_principles: Some top floor traders made their money fading large spikes up or down (buying the bottom of a flush when many are trapped), contrary to 'never fade' folklore; rules are flexible by trader.
Do not exit a strong trend trade early just because the P&L looks big ('if the train is going to California don't get off in Chicago').
Avoid carrying large option positions into December/holiday illiquidity; short-premium books can lose years of gains quickly.
Vol products (VIX curve, term structure) tend to react first; watching them helps time ES even if you do not trade them.
Common trait of great traders: unflappable, even-keeled under loss; humour as a stress outlet.
New retail traders should treat trading as a part-time job with other income to remove pressure.
notes: Colourful floor-trading war stories (eurodollar pit, Amaranth blowup). Current approach (VIX term structure spreads vs ES levels, wait for extremes) described only vaguely; no concrete setups.

style: fund (Ambrus Group long-volatility tail-risk fund) with intraday flow-based absolute-return book; ex-prop (Chimera)
markets: SPX/VIX options, variance swaps, US stocks intraday
edge_principles: Fund tail hedges (sub-5-delta 1-3 month options, ~10% of AUM) with uncorrelated intraday flow strategies that are flat by the close, rather than by selling concave short-vol structures.
Execution price matters enormously on cheap tails: filling at 5c instead of 20c turns a 5x into a 20x payoff.
Research hygiene: start from a thesis, use 3-4 features max, keep an untouched out-of-sample set; avoid iterative 'what if I had done X' overfitting.
Technical patterns can be valid as the visual form of underlying flow/statistical effects (e.g. VWAP crossovers after institutional buying ends).
Size with fractional Kelly plus a hard cap; scale up slowly when trading well and down when trading poorly.
Markets are not Gaussian; mean-reversion trades that assume known sigma levels are dangerous.
notes: Long-vol fund manager. One concrete intraday flow pattern: large opening drop on bad news attracts dip-buying via MOO/VWAP orders for ~first hour, then fades all day.

style: systematic trend follower; ran a manual DAX warrant volatility arbitrage 2015-2019
markets: German DAX bank-issued warrants vs Eurex DAX options
edge_principles: Structural edges come from counterparties' operational constraints (stale vol surfaces, too-tight retail spreads), not prediction; they decay once the counterparty notices (spread 1c->2c killed it).
Measure relative cheapness intraday with rolling percentiles of the spread to fair value and only act in the extreme decile plus a catalyst (market move).
Paper-trade ~100-200 instances to rehearse execution before going live on an execution-sensitive edge.
Commission and spread sensitivity is decisive for very short holding periods; shop execution venues.
Hide footprint: split legs across counterparties.
notes: Detailed account of a niche retail-structured-product volatility arbitrage. Not transferable to MCF data, recorded for completeness and as an example of a structural edge and its decay.

style: retail, discretionary sector-relative stock trader since the 1990s; now crypto/DeFi yield
edge_principles: Never meet a margin call; exit instead (a short that tripled on fluff news would have wiped him out even though the stock later went to zero).
Follow the stop side of the trading plan rigidly; allow flexibility only on the profit side.
Time stop: exit if the position has not moved above entry within a set period.
Scale in small (e.g. 10% of intended size) and add only as the position proves itself.
Avoid buying stocks in steady downtrends; wait for a bottom/rebound and a catalyst.
Big early wins breed overconfidence and oversizing; behaviour before blow-ups (revenge trading, bigger size, faster trading) is predictable.
notes: New host introduction interview. One loosely specified idea: sector leader moves first and laggards follow days later.

style: fund/CTA, contrarian positioning trader (COT-based) with discretionary overlay
markets: futures: stock indices, currencies, bonds, commodities
edge_principles: Use participation (money actually committed, e.g. COT speculator positioning indexed to its own history) as the discounting mechanism, not price or surveys.
Never act on the crowding signal alone; wait for market confirmation (a news-failure event).
Win rate ~37% with ~4:1 payoff is enough; accept repeated stop-outs while the crowded condition persists.
Treat highly correlated positions as one trade and cut per-trade risk accordingly.
Exit when the crowd is no longer crowded (positioning mean-reverts to neutral) rather than riding to the opposite extreme; volatility rises faster than return after neutral.
His fully systematic version underperformed his discretionary-overlay version; he skips ~20-25% of system signals in known weak spots.
Patience pays: a month away from the screen with a stop made more than a year of in-and-out trading.
notes: Unknown Market Wizards contrarian. Core idea: fade extreme speculator positioning only after a bearish (bullish) headline fails to move price; holds 2-4 months.

style: crypto infrastructure founder (bloXroute), not a trader
edge_principles: Small accounts that churn in and out of trends lose; larger capital held with patience behaves better (he lost by trading instead of holding).
In DeFi, transaction costs are large relative to small positions, which forces fewer, larger moves.
Concentrated AMM liquidity provision is economically a short option (like selling puts/calls in a range); you end up holding the losing asset when price exits the range.
Speed of information (network latency) is an edge in on-chain trading, as in traditional HFT.
notes: DeFi primer (AMMs, liquidity provision, staking, the Merge). No trading setups.

style: retail/small fund FX trader using proprietary retail-positioning and stop-cluster data ('market causality'); also runs ~8 automated FX bots
edge_principles: Retail ('dumb money') tends to try reversals/mean-reversion and place stops just beyond the obvious recent high/low; those clusters get run before the real move.
Expect several counter-moves (he estimates 8-10) and long sideways time before the main run to a known stop cluster; enter with limit orders on counter-moves rather than chasing.
On news, price often spikes to take a nearby stop cluster then reverses back toward where crowded positions are trapped.
Always use a stop (or hedge) and low leverage; going stopless to avoid hunts leads to blowups.
Automated strategies: aim for net profit 2-4x max drawdown over ~8 years of data including variable spread, slippage and commissions; avoid commercial EAs (often martingale).
Stand aside when it is unclear which way the dominant players will push.
notes: Forex 'stop hunting' / smart-money narrative relying on proprietary retail positioning feeds. One price-only analogue (failed range break after stop run) is testable on stocks/ETFs.

style: fund (two small options hedge funds), systematic option seller
edge_principles: 'Expectancy hacking': fix the win/loss size ratio mechanically (profit target and stop as % of credit), then only the win rate determines expectancy; verify it is above break-even by backtest and live trading.
Bake slippage and gap-through-stop losses into the expected loss size instead of rejecting stops.
Credit targeting: size each entry to a constant premium/risk amount (fewer contracts when IV is high) to remove sequence/path risk from variable trade sizes.
Top-down sizing: annual P&L target / expected capture rate / number of trading days = per-trade risk budget.
A stop is just an exposure adjustment; systematic re-entry each day is equivalent to rolling.
Know total open risk: if every open position hit its stop, what % of the account would be lost.
Volatility drag: large drawdowns destroy compounding regardless of edge, so size for the path not only the destination.
notes: Systematic SPX short-put programme with mechanical profit-take and stop; mostly options-specific risk management lessons.
